opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (employee ID E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E017.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jennifer Miller (E017) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write (admin requires owning role, which is Engineer; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level equals maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jennifer Miller (E017) is a contractor with basic security training (note says full-time, but Security DB is authoritative for employment type). Contractor policy: read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Basic training => max read. Requested write is above max, so recommend read.
reason: Jennifer Miller (E017) requested write access to Source Code. HR's note says full-time (max write), but Security agent's note states that Security DB (authoritative for employment type) shows contractor with basic security training. Under contractor policy, read is the maximum (write requires advanced training; never admin). Since requested write exceeds the maximum of read, the granted level is read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket carefully.

The ticket: Jennifer Miller (E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- HR agent: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommends write (full-time max is write; Analyst doesn't own Source Code so no admin).
- Security agent: role Analyst, employment type contractor with basic security training, recommends read. Security says their DB is authoritative for employment type, and contractor with basic training => max read.

Conflicting information: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Both looked up in their own databases. Security says their DB is authoritative for employment type.

Which to trust? The notes say HR looked up employment type in own database; Security looked up in own database and claims Security DB is authoritative for employment type. There's a conflict. The Approver must decide.

Typically in these tasks, the security agent's note is authoritative for security-related info (employment type per security DB). The security agent says contractor with basic training => max read.

The policy: contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training => read max.

Requested write is above max => grant max = read.

I'll submit decision: read.

Let me provide reasoning.
